_comment: Case pack for CASE 003 / OPERATION FRONT ROW. Same schema as case-001-maya.json. Note: this is the only case whose brief is explicitly two-sided — it asks for a creator-side decision AND an audience-side next step. Transcribed from docs/evidence/case-003-operation-front-row.txt.

case.logline: A 320K creator with a permanent seat at the centre of European tech. Thirteen million views. One person who cannot be in two rooms at once.
case.mission: Help Aditi decide what to make next: content that builds real trust with her audience, not just reach, and gives them a clear next step to take.
case.ask: Build one working product that helps Aditi decide what to make next, AND gives her audience a clear next step to take.
judged_on: Value to a real audience member
case.final_line_template: Aditi no longer needs to ____ because ____.
explicitly_not: Not a better link in bio.

creator.name: Aditi Mishra
creator.role: Creator, host and Head of New Media at a European tech title
creator.business: Brand + hosting + advisory; keynotes, MC work, live founder interviews
creator.reputation: Aditi's audience treats her as the person already sitting in the room they are trying to get into. They believe she will tell them what it actually took, and what she would do in their position.
creator.assessment: Her access is the asset, but only if she can tell people what to do with it. The content problem and the trust problem are the same problem: one clear, repeatable answer, not a faster way to reply to everyone separately.

voice._source: E-05.7 thought process + E-05.5 margin note
voice.voice_note: I actually like answering people. It's why the community feels like a community. What I can't do is be awake in six countries at once. If something could capture how I decide, not just where I happened to be standing, that would be useful to a lot more people than the ones who catch me live.
notice_this: not just where I happened to be standing
awake in six countries at once
the ones who catch me live
voice.her_rule: I would rather say one true thing about a room I was actually in than ten clever things about a room I was not.
voice.creed: People want my judgement, not my calendar.
style_rules: If I would not say it to my sister on the phone, I do not post it.
She will publicly name the opportunities she said no to.
She values the honest arithmetic of what something cost over the glamour of having been there.

unfinished_ideas: let people bring me their own decision
maybe the answer is not a newsletter
decision_rules.contradiction: She keeps saying 'less content'. But her highest-converting posts are also the most heavily edited. The opportunity may be less about posting less and more about making each judgement carry more of her context.

shelf.maya_note: the best answer I ever gave

shelf_assessment: Extract: 8 of 61 assets. Being in the room is not the same thing as an answer. Useful fields: Room, Format, Decision, Cost, Aditi rating, Personal note, 'Would I do it again?'

personas_note: The audience does not behave like one audience. Large enough to be a real audience. Specific enough that one generic answer fails all of them.

tracked_individuals.profile: Wants the route in, not the story. Watches six times, saves, then researches alone.

tracked_individuals.name: Jamie
tracked_individuals.profile: Already in tech. Wants Aditi's framing applied to his own decision. Returns to old posts and asks follow-ups.

tracked_individuals.name: Priya

tracked_individuals.name: Ella

inbox_clue: Twelve messages, seven different jobs. Underneath all of them: decide for me the way you would decide for yourself.

broadcast_log.title: The three questions I ask before I post anything
Everything I saw at Cannes Lions
What that week actually cost me
The answer I gave a founder backstage
The opportunities I said no to this year

broadcast_clue: 3.9M views produced 62 sign-ups. 320K views produced 806. Read the behaviour, not the vanity metric.

field_notes_tuesday.detail: Lighting, outfit and lines set from memory
Editorial and new media, full attention
Reads three founder decks between meetings

field_notes_tuesday.what: Voice notes on the walk home

field_notes_tuesday.detail: 900 words so he can cut without her
Country four of six, four months
Tomorrow I need to fix this.

field_notes_clue: Two DM sprints a day and the queue still grows. The bottleneck is not effort. Her judgement exists only in real time, and only in one place at a time.

intelligence_drop_1600.headline: THE OPPORTUNITY IS ALMOST NEVER THE CLICK
intelligence_drop_1600.detail: People use Aditi to decide, then act weeks later, usually somewhere she cannot see. The value is being undercounted by every obvious metric.

hidden_audience.look_closer: The YES/NO around link clicks is intentionally incomplete. You are supposed to decide what matters, then decide what to instrument. Signal can be behavioural rather than transactional.

build_must: Help a real audience member make a better decision.
Preserve a meaningful piece of Aditi's judgement and taste.
Be demonstrable in a few clicks.
Not require expensive AI inference to be impressive.
mission_framing: Your mission is not to build a better link in bio, or a course. It is to turn Aditi's judgement into one answer her audience can trust, and know exactly what to do with.
